host.label: Host name or IP address
host.help: Address of the router web interface, for example 192.168.1.1
host.validatorErrorText: A host name or IP address is required

port.label: Port
port.help: Port of the web interface. Switching HTTPS moves this between the two defaults, 80 and 443; a port you set yourself, such as 8080, is left alone.

https.label: Use HTTPS
https.help: Only enable this if the router web interface is configured for TLS

allowSelfSigned.label: Accept a self-signed certificate
allowSelfSigned.help: FreshTomato ships a self-signed certificate, which is rejected by default. Enabling this encrypts the traffic but no longer verifies the identity of the router, which leaves room for a machine-in-the-middle.

httpId.label: HTTP ID
httpId.help: Router UI: Administration → Admin Access → Web Admin ID. Starts with TID.
httpId.validatorErrorText: The HTTP ID is required; without it the router closes the connection without answering

pollInterval.label: Poll interval (seconds)
pollInterval.validatorErrorText: The poll interval must be between 10 and 600 seconds
pollInterval.help: How often the router is queried. Values between 10 and 600 seconds.

requestTimeout.label: Request timeout (seconds)
requestTimeout.validatorErrorText: The request timeout must be between 5 and 120 seconds
requestTimeout.help: How long a single request to the router may take. Raise it for an older router or a slow link; the per-address traffic page is the slow one and has been measured at 19 s on a WNR3500L. A timeout is also what a name lookup that never returns looks like.

offlineTimeout.label: Offline timeout (seconds)
offlineTimeout.validatorErrorText: The offline timeout must be between 0 and 3600 seconds
offlineTimeout.help: A device is marked offline this many seconds after its last sign of life — a wireless association or a change in its traffic counters. This bridges short gaps and lets stale ARP entries settle to offline. 0 marks a device offline as soon as a poll shows no activity.

createDeviceObjects.label: Create one channel per connected device
createDeviceObjects.help: Turn this off on busy networks. The device list stays available as JSON under devices.json. Per-device traffic logging needs these channels: each device gets a writable trafficEnabled switch in the object tree.

allowReboot.label: Allow rebooting the router
allowReboot.help: Without this the reboot state exists but cannot be written. A reboot takes every device in the network off the internet for a minute or more.

influxInstance.label: InfluxDB instance
influxInstance.help: The InfluxDB adapter does the logging with its own credentials. Pick its instance here, or 'disabled'. The freshtomato instance must be running for this list to load.

influxPrefix.label: Datapoint prefix
influxPrefix.help: Stored as the InfluxDB alias, e.g. prefix 'freshtomato' -> freshtomato.system.load1. Empty stores under the real datapoint id.

logSystem.label: Log system KPIs (CPU temperature, load, memory)

logNetwork.label: Log network KPIs (WAN reachable, interface rx/tx bytes)

logWlan.label: Log WLAN KPIs (client count, radio temperature, noise)
